title: L2-ARCTIC: A Non-Native English Speech Corpus
manual_evidence: Corpus documentation reports 24 non-native speakers, roughly one hour of read speech per speaker, and a manually annotated subset of about 150 utterances per speaker. The manual subset has corrected word and phone boundaries plus phone substitution, deletion and addition tags; current corpus documentation and the Lhotse recipe enumerate 3,599 manual annotations across 24 speakers, with approximately 9,458 phone segments in the manual subset.
inclusion_rationale: Primary non-singing L2 production with phone-level human correction and categorical production-error judgments, valuable for timing, segment realization, error and L1-effects analyses.
decision_note: Only the manually corrected subset is eligible for core. Corpus-wide forced-aligned word/phone tiers that were not manually corrected must remain excluded. Access is mediated by the corpus download form/license, so no files are redistributed until terms and file-level provenance are checked.
next_action: Resolve corpus license and obtain authoritative download; enumerate all speaker directories and TextGrids; isolate the manually annotated ~150 utterances per speaker; ingest corrected word/phone intervals, error tiers/comments, transcripts, speaker L1/gender metadata and file checksums while retaining forced-aligned-only material as ineligible lineage metadata.
dedup_note: No current registry hit found for L2-ARCTIC. Deduplicate only within its own corpus lineage; the manual subset and automatic tiers are alternate annotation layers over the same recordings, not separate productions.

title: Corpus of European Portuguese Stops
manual_evidence: Author documentation states that 54 real-word stop stimuli were produced by six native speakers, both in isolation and a carrier sentence, and manually segmented. Corpus-2 .seg files encode eight human-defined acoustic/EGG landmarks (preceding-vowel onset, closure onset, prevoicing onset, voice offset, prevoicing end/burst, release onset, following-vowel onset, following-vowel offset), plus word position and a four-level voicing classification; paired .ipa files contain SAMPA transcriptions.
inclusion_rationale: Primary non-singing production with unusually rich manually located temporal landmarks and simultaneous laryngograph signal, directly useful for VOT, closure, release, prevoicing and vowel-duration analyses.
decision_note: The authoritative page describes distribution on CD-ROM rather than providing an openly downloadable research archive or clear redistribution license. Preserve as review until file-level public access/rights can be resolved; do not reconstruct landmark observations from published summary statistics.
next_action: Locate an authoritative public mirror/deposit or obtain permitted access; inventory .wav/.seg/.ipa files; preserve the eight original landmark times and zero-as-not-observed convention, position and voicing codes, SAMPA, speaker/dialect metadata, EGG/acoustic equipment and checksums; derive durations only in separate fields.
dedup_note: No current registry hit found for this corpus. Related publications analyze the same recordings and must link to this single recording lineage rather than create duplicate datasets.
